texts.preamble: Rohini. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024
texts.facts: (l) It is pertinent to mention that the Appellants had challenged the impugned order before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Crl.P No. 5527/2024. So, on the above mentioned grounds, the appellant has requested to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the trial Court order dated 06.05.2024. So, the notice was issued to the respondent. In response to the notice, the respondent entered his appearance through learned counsel. 4. After having gone through the records, this Court felt that there is an element of settlement, therefore, the Court has made a sincere effort to settle the dispute, between the parties amicably. At one point of time, almost the matter was about to be settled, but unfortunately, the same not ended in settlement. 9. The rank of the parties have been referred as stated in the present appeal. Upon perusal of records, it is evident that the specific allegations made by the appellant is that the appellant is unable to maintain herself as she is in financial doldrums as she has to financially sustain her children and herself to pay interest to the loans, to pay rents on monthly basis for her present residence and also she has to meet out the education expenses of her children. Therefore, the appellant constrained to seek the reliefs sought in the interlocutory applications. It is further alleged that the appellant has to bear the education expenses of her Crl.A.No.1303/2024 children to the extent of Rs.1,01,883/- per month. But the respondent has been contributing only to the extent of Rs.60,000/- per month. The rest of the amount is being paid by the appellant. It is contended that the Appellant is currently residing at the address mentioned in the cause title. The Appellant and Respondent have been married since 18.08.2006. The marriage is also registered under the Hindu Marriage Act. The Appellant B.M. Rohini and the Respondent have two children Anya and Arnav aged 16 and 14. years respectively from the said marriage. Almost immediately after moving into the matrimonial house, the Respondent who was ably influenced by his parents created a very hostile environment at the matrimonial home and tortured the Appellant by using profane and vulgar language. The matrimonial house is a 3 floor house consisting of 7 bedrooms where the Appellant, Respondent and his parents resided. The Appellant was constantly humiliated/belittled and insulted by the Respondent and his parents with condescending and snide remarks being made about her and her family. At the time of marriage the Respondent's parents demanded Crl.A.No.1303/2024 the Appellant's father to pay Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs only) in cash as dowry and they even went to the extent of threatening to cancel the wedding if he refused. Fearing that they would call off the wedding, the Appellant's father had no other choice but to oblige to their demands. The Appellant was unaware that her father was forced to pay the aforementioned dowry at the time of marriage and she was shocked to find out the same only after her marriage to the Respondent. The Appellant immediately confronted the Respondent and his parents about the dowry and demanded that it be returned to her father. Upon confrontation, the Respondent and his parents instantly turned hostile and hurled abuses at the Appellant and she was shocked and petrified when her brother-in-law raised his hand in an attempt to hit her without any provocation from her side Rohini. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51896706/ 10 whatsoever. This incident caused a lot of discord between the Appellant and the rest of the Respondent's family and she feared for her Crl.A.No.1303/2024 safety in the matrimonial house. It was only after repeated confrontations did the Parents of the Respondent agree to return around Rs. 11,00,000/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs only) by transferring it to the Appellant's bank account which was only a fraction of the dowry paid by her father. Owing to the aforementioned incident, the Appellant was never whole heartedly accepted by the Respondent's family and it manifested in hostile treatment meted out to the Appellant by the Respondent and his family as well. 4. Since the Appellant was the only person who did not follow 'Kalki Bhagwan', she was constantly made to feel worthless. The Respondent and his family constantly made comparisons between the Appellant and her co-sister, and repeatedly praised her co-sister in front of guests. In fact, the Respondent would completely ignore the Appellant and go to his co-sister for every advice including decisions involving their own children. Over time the Respondent and the Appellant Crl.A.No.1303/2024 would spend less and less time together as a family and the Respondent spent more time with his parents, brother and co-sister and it became evident that Respondent had no interest in spending time with the Appellant or their children. In fact, the Respondent would make deliberate efforts to ignore the Appellant and their children, the Respondent would either shrug them away by lecturing them that he had to work hard to earn money or he would purposely put his headphones on and begin chanting and praying at random hours of the day, he would even sleep as early as 8:30 PM and make no attempt to interact with the Appellant or their children. 5. The Respondent is a partner of the illustrious "B.V. Aswathiah & Bros. (Regd)", a partnership firm established in the year 1936 which is engaged in the business of manufacture and export of 'Nandi' brand agarbattis, coils, dhoops and perfumes etc. The said partnership firm is a leading agarbatti manufacturer Crl.A.No.1303/2024 and exporter in India, it has 6 manufacturing units spread over an area of over 50,000 Sq.ft, and it has a production capacity of 1000 tons per year. It is submitted that apart from the monthly income earnings from the partnership firm the Respondent also earns huge amounts as rents from commercial and residential properties owned and let out on rent by the Respondent. Further, the Respondent is an entrepreneur and also earns income from the multiple businesses he runs. Even though the Respondent Crl.A.No.1303/2024 worked for the joint family business and earned sufficient money to provide a normal lifestyle, the Respondent's brother who did not work, fixed the monthly allowance for the Respondent, Appellant and their two children at Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand only) and they were expected to manage all their expenses within that amount. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51896706/ 11 all-round development. Such being the case, the Appellant being a housewife was forced Crl.A.No.1303/2024 to be at the mercy of her brother and aged parents for expenses. 7. It is contended that on one occasion, the Respondent encouraged their daughter to join a short course on fashion designing as she intended to pursue a career in it and when the time came to pay for the said course, the Respondent suddenly backed out of the responsibility to pay even though the Respondent could afford it. Similarly, the Respondent himself listed all the design schools their daughter could go to abroad and the moment he found out that it would cost more than Rs.1 Crore, the Respondent immediately backed out stating that Respondent can only spend Rs.1 Lakh on her education. The Respondent would refuse to take the Appellant and their children out for dinners, movies, vacations etc. and would only agree to come and spend time with them if the Appellant would pay for it. Such instances which were done deliberately by the Respondent would Crl.A.No.1303/2024 bring down the morale of the young children and they were often left inconsolable as their own father Le., the Respondent refused to provide for them. The Respondent would force the Appellant to take care of the children and drop them to school and take care of all the domestic chores on her own, while the Respondent claimed to be at work. Even though the Respondent and his family were aware that the Appellant was not well, they left her alone at home and went to the Kalki Bhagwan Ashram in utter disregard of her mental and physical state. The Appellant felt so Crl.A.No.1303/2024 dejected by this incident that she decided to leave the matrimonial home with her children. As she was leaving home with the children with suitcases in her hand, the Appellant's father-in-law who was returning home from the ashram sarcastically remarked, "All the best kids, enjoy!". In 2021, the Appellant and Respondent eventually moved into an apartment away from the Respondent's family which they took on rent with the help of the Respondents uncle who paid the advance amount.
texts.arguments: It is also contended that though the respondent had agreed to pay Rs.1,50,000/- per month as a monthly maintenance, but he is deliberately avoiding from his responsibilities. 10. It is also specifically alleged that the appellant has no other place for her stay with children except the matrimonial home. The said matrimonial home is consisting of three floors having seven bed rooms, but, the appellant and her children were forced to vacate the said matrimonial home. The respondent and his family members have tortured the appellant physically, verbally, emotionally and economically. Therefore, the appellant is constrained to file the petition for seeking maintenance towards eduction expenses, medical expenses and payment towards Crl.A.No.1303/2024 rent. So, the respondent has to pay Rs.1,45,000/- towards rent of her residence. 11. On the other hand, the respondent entered his appearance through his learned counsel and supported the findings of the trial Court and sought for rejection of the present appeal. The Appellant is unemployed and is a housewife and is wholly dependent on the Respondent and the Appellant's family members for her day to day expenses. 6. It is contended that despite being wealthy, the Respondent and his household was accounted for. Every time a purchase was made it would be deducted from the said Rs.40,000/- and no one was not allowed to spend any amount in excess of it. When the Appellant requested him to buy her a car to drop and pick up their children from school, the Respondent refused to buy her a car stating that the Respondent cannot afford it even though the Respondent was more than capable of affording the same. The Appellant's father had to step in and buy the Appellant a car for her daily use. 8. It is contended that though the Appellant and the Respondent resided together in the matrimonial house, there was virtually no marital relationship between them due to the Respondent's indifference towards the Appellant and their children. 9. It is contended that the cruelty the Appellant was subjected to by the Respondent and his family, was so extreme that there have been times of medical emergencies when they refused to pay for it. The Respondent and his family abandoned the Appellant when she was in no position to look after herself. The Appellant was shocked when the Respondent refused to even pay for the hospital expenses stating that there was no money left from the monthly allowance of Rs.40,000/- and she was left with no other option but to borrow money from her parents who live in Hyderabad. It is contended that since the Appellant is a housewife and she has no source of income to Crl.A.No.1303/2024 maintain herself and her children, the Appellant is dependent on her brother and her parents who are senior citizens for the Appellants day to day expenses.
